I couldn't find the GitHub app by searching the App Store; had to use the direct link from the blog post to install it.
Tried the iOS beta and didn't find a single bug; enjoyed using it for casually browsing code on my phone.
Trying to follow a link on a README or file within a repo always results in a 'something went wrong' error on iOS.
On Android, code review is hampered: diff lines wrap due to large code font, per-commit review is hard to use, and the main activity feed from '/' is missing.
Following a link to a specific issue comment (e.g., from a notification email) just lands you at the top of the issue instead of the comment.
The app let me sign in without 2FA even though it's enabled org-wide; turned out it was reusing a browser token—re-signing in triggered the 2FA prompt correctly.
Clicking a GitHub link to a new repo on Android repeatedly asks whether to open it in Chrome or the GitHub app for every single repo, which is very annoying.
Push notifications work well overall, but there's no notification for being assigned to review a PR, which is frustrating.
Wished the app supported multiple accounts (e.g., personal and work), assuming it was a planned feature.
On first glance it looked nice on the iPad.
Wished the commit feed would be replaced with a PR comment feed, since the unit of review is the PR, not individual commits, and commit noise isn't useful.
Called the new mobile app 'a step in the wrong direction from work/life balance.'
GitHub's separate mobile website is praised as one of the better implementations—optimized for touch, covers most features, and easily switches to desktop site.
Complained that the mobile website's diff view is unusable, along with many other views, preferring a working web version over a dedicated app.
After years of waiting for a mobile GitHub experience, still on the beta waitlist and defaulting to 'Request Desktop Site' in mobile browsers as the main workaround.
Received an invite to test the iOS beta but couldn't use it because their account was incorrectly flagged as spam after reporting spammers, blocking use of the app entirely.
